title: His standards for the band and objections to drinking
summary: Lewis liked Lawrence Marrero and Louis Nelson, was a perfectionist and born leader, gave up leading when ill, and disliked musicians playing drunk.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Did he have any special favorites among the musicians or did he say anything about that?

Well, as far as favorites, there were no special favorites. Naturally, he liked Lawrence Moreiro. But Lawrence is gone. And he was getting a little bit displeased with the musicians toward the end because he was a perfectionist in his playing. George wanted everything to be just so. He really was a born leader when it came to a band. And it hurt him deeply when he became ill and couldn't lead, couldn't be a leader. I mean, he turned that down himself because he felt it wasn't fair to the group that since he couldn't lead, be the leader, it wouldn't give the men the opportunity to play as often. He didn't believe in all the drinking that had been going on because when he played for the public, he wanted to give his best and he wanted the musicians to do their best. Sometimes alcohol just doesn't mix. And the true playing. He didn't want to be mocked. He said he just didn't want to be mocked. He said people are coming. He said there may be, most of them are tourists, true. He said, but there are true purists that come in. And if they hear the music played in the manner it's played when the men are heavily intoxicated. He said, they allow him to make a remark. He said, and he doesn't like any remarks given out because there's no need for it. He knows the capability of some musicians that they can do had they not been in this condition. I mean, he liked Louie Nelson's playing. And he liked all the musicians playing as far as their playing goes. I'm not saying, I'm not going to say many of the remarks he made toward the end simply because I have a feeling that he didn't mean some of it that he had said.
Yeah, well, it's just better not playing again.
